title: James Bond in the Yookay
author: Dominic Green
content:
![James Bond in the
Yookay](https://storage.ghost.io/c/65/af/65afbdb5-30bf-4286-acc4-9535069adb42/content/images/2026/11/IMG_5447-1-1.jpg)

Mr. Bond, we've been expecting you. For five years, since 2021's _No Time To
Die_. After Daniel Craig's final and overextended turn in the black tuxedo, it
was past time for his James Bond to die. Outmanned by Jason Bourne's supremacy
and unmanned by the psychic confessional of _Skyfall_ (2012), the sixth 007
became the first to die on the job. At the end of _No Time To Die_ , Craig
became a human target marker, blown to bits by a shower of cruise missiles.
The critics were little kinder: The Bond franchise needed a mercy killing.

Yet Bond is back, with Denis Villeneuve, skilled at a slick epic, directing
the saturnine Robert Pattinson. Bond never lived, so he cannot die. Like
Sherlock Holmes, he lives in the imagination, and that makes him more real
than most real people. His translation from books to screen proved that you
can, as it happens, live twice. But his life has lately undergone a further
translation. From 1962's _Dr. No_ until _No Time to Die_ , the Bond movies
were produced in Britain by Albert "Cubby" Broccoli's Eon Productions. When
Broccoli died in 1997, his stepson Michael G. Wilson and his daughter Barbara
took over. In February 2025, Wilson and Barbara Broccoli [_sold creative
control_](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c1mn9gz5x3mo?ref=compactmag.com)
of the Bond franchise to Amazon MGM Studios. Bond, the personification of an
ideal from twentieth-century Britain, is now an American idol. Can Bond live
for a third time?
